title: When parsing a report descriptor, Delimiter items cause usages and controls to get out of sync
body:
The HID spec section 6.2.2.8 states:

> Two or more alternative usages may be associated with a control by simply bracketing them with Delimiter items. Delimiters allow aliases to be defined for a control so that an application can access it in more than one way. The usages that form a delimited set are organized in order of preference, where the first usage declared is the most preferred usage for the control.
>
> HID parsers must handle Delimiters however, the support for the alternative usages that they define is optional. Usages other than the first (most preferred) usage defined may not be made accessible by system software.

However, the WebHID spec does not handle Delimiter tags specifically, and so all of the usages inside a Delimiter get put into `usages`, and they're "used up" one at a time.

I think it's OK to not support anything after the first usage inside a Delimiter, but we should probably ignore subsequent ones instead of putting them into `usages`.

---

Recommended spec changes:

1. Add a definition for the **Delimiter tag** alongside the other local item tags. Also add Delimiter to the non-normative note that lists the local items: "An item with the Delimiter tag opens (item data 1) or closes (item data 0) a set of alternative usages for a single control."

2. In "parse the report descriptor", after "Initialize stringIndices to be an empty list.", add:

   > Initialize inDelimitedSet to false.
   >
   > Initialize delimitedUsageSeen to false.

3. In the Main item branch, after "Set usages to be an empty sequence of `unsigned long`.", add:

   > Set inDelimitedSet to false.
   >
   > Set delimitedUsageSeen to false.

4. In the Local item branch, after "Let value be the item data field interpreted as an `unsigned long`.", insert:

   > 1. If item has the Delimiter tag:
   >     1. If value is 1, set inDelimitedSet to true and set delimitedUsageSeen to false.
   >     2. Otherwise, if value is 0, set inDelimitedSet to false.
   >     3. Continue.
   > 2. If inDelimitedSet is true, delimitedUsageSeen is true, and item has the Usage tag, Usage Minimum tag, or Usage Maximum tag, then continue.
   >
   >     Note: Delimited sets list alternative usages for a single control in order of preference. Only the first, most preferred, usage of each set is kept, as permitted by [USBIF-HID-CLASS] section 6.2.2.8.

5. In the same branch, at the end of the existing Usage tag step (after "Append value to usages") and at the end of the existing Usage Maximum tag step, add:

   > If inDelimitedSet is true, set delimitedUsageSeen to true.

   The Usage Minimum step deliberately does not set the flag. That way the first alias can be a Usage Minimum / Usage Maximum pair, and both halves are kept.
